territorial_scope.description: Applies within the State of Oregon, as an act of the Oregon Legislature.

evidence.quote: Be It Enacted by the People of the State of Oregon

summary.short: Oregon SB 1571 (2024) requires any campaign communication that includes synthetic media of an individual, meaning a realistic but false AI-manipulated depiction, to carry a disclosure that it has been manipulated. Certain providers and publishers are exempt. The act takes effect on passage.
summary.long: SB 1571 (2024) adds a section to Oregon's election chapter (ORS chapter 260) on AI-manipulated media in campaign communications. Synthetic media is an image, audio or video recording of an individual, intentionally manipulated with artificial intelligence or similar digital technology, that creates a realistic but false depiction materially different from the original. A campaign communication supporting or opposing a clearly identified candidate or measure that includes any synthetic media must include a disclosure stating the recording has been manipulated. Exemptions cover interactive computer and information service providers; broadcasters and publishers carrying bona fide news coverage with authenticity acknowledgments or non-representation statements; paid broadcasts or publications under stated conditions; and satire or parody. The Secretary of State or Attorney General may seek injunctions in circuit court without proof of injury, and the prevailing party recovers reasonable attorney fees. On proof of a violation, the court imposes a civil penalty of up to $10,000, paid to the General Fund. This remedy is exclusive. ORS 260.345 is amended to route complaints and enforcement for these violations, with a 90-day filing limit for electors. The Secretary of State may adopt implementing rules. The act takes effect on passage under an emergency declaration.

relations.note: Section 3 amends ORS 260.345 and reproduces the amended section in full. The document does not mark which wording is new, so the changed subsections cannot be separated from unchanged text.
Section 1 is added to and made a part of ORS chapter 260 by Section 2.

evidence.quote: Section 1 of this 2024 Act is added to and made a part of ORS chapter 260.

relations.note: Section 1 uses the ORS 260.005 (10)(c) definition of 'clearly identified candidate or measure' for 'campaign communication'. Section 1(1)(a)(B) states that, notwithstanding ORS 260.005 (10)(c)(B)(i), aggregate expenditures of any amount are allowed.

Section 3 gives the Secretary of State civil proceedings for violations under ORS 260.537 and sends prosecution, penalty and time-limit questions for violations under section 1 through the same mechanism.

evidence.quote: In the case of a violation under ORS 260.537, may institute civil proceedings in the manner described in ORS 260.537

relations.note: Section 3(4)(a) routes violations subject to a penalty under ORS 260.993 to the Attorney General for prosecution. Section 3(4)(b) excludes those violations from the administrative civil penalty under ORS 260.995.

evidence.quote: In the case of a violation that is subject to a penalty under ORS 260.993

relations.note: Section 3(4)(b) lets the Secretary of State impose a civil penalty under ORS 260.995 for violations not subject to ORS 260.537, ORS 260.993 or section 1. Section 3(6) gives the Attorney General the same power.

evidence.quote: may impose a civil penalty under ORS 260.995

relations.note: Section 3(8) sets limitation periods for filing officers, subject to an exception in ORS 260.234. The text does not state what that exception provides.
Section 1(6)(a) excludes providers of an interactive computer service as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230(f) from the section's scope.
Section 1(6)(a) excludes providers of an information service as defined in 47 U.S.C. 153 from the section's scope.

evidence.quote: as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230(f), or an information service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. 153

notes: Section 1(1)(a)(B) overrides ORS 260.005 (10)(c)(B)(i) for campaign communications. Section 3(4)(b) contains a bracketed [or] in the printed text, which is reproduced as shown. Section 1(4) says the court 'shall impose' the penalty of not more than $10,000, while Section 3(4)(d) says the Secretary of State 'may institute' civil proceedings. The document gives no enactment or effective date beyond the emergency clause, which takes effect on passage (Section 5). Section 4 grants rulemaking power to the Secretary of State for Section 1, so no instrument is cited as legal basis.
